_what: Drives docs/phase2/forge.mjs. Same shape as reference-manifest.json: prose lives in _-prefixed keys so the file stays readable without a second doc that can drift from it.
_scope: KAIDA ONLY. Vex, Rune and the grunt wait until she is signed off — docs/phase2/README.md §Rules that must not drift, rule 1. Their refs already exist; adding them here is a human decision, not a convenience.
_out: Working directory for intermediate meshes and the stage hash cache. Gitignored — a 15-minute regeneration is cheaper than a churning binary in git history.
_assets: Where `install` puts the character the game actually loads: assets/<name>.glb + assets/<name>.bones.json, at the GAME ROOT, not public/. Vite full-page-reloads on any publicDir change, which would defeat the hot swap. See vite.config.js.
_stages: Run in this order. Each skips when every output exists and sha256(input bytes + that stage's config below) matches out/.hashes.json. --force overrides.
_venv: Python 3.10, NOT the system 3.14: the Hunyuan MLX port tests on 3.10 and torch's cp314 wheel is not what it was built against (README §Stage 1). Both stages below refuse to guess at a CLI nobody has run — they print the exact command instead.

mesh._precision: INT8 ≈ 6 GB peak. FP16 ≈ 10 GB is too tight on 16 GB unified with Vite and Chrome resident; INT4 ≈ 4 GB is the fallback if INT8 thrashes. README §Stage 1 has the table and the models already ruled out — do not re-investigate TRELLIS, Stable Fast 3D, TripoSR or any paid service.
mesh._duration: ~9 min for 6 views at 512 on an M2 Pro; expect longer on an M1 Pro. Wall-clock is not a constraint — unattended overnight runs are the intended mode.

rig._model: UniRig — https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/UniRig. SIGGRAPH 2025, VAST-AI. Predicts skeleton hierarchy AND per-vertex skinning weights. Components are released progressively; verify what actually exists before assuming this stage can run at all.
rig._fallback: Mixamo's free auto-rigger is a manual browser fallback. It still feeds `install` — drop its output at out/<name>-rigged.glb and run `--stage install`.
rig._acceptance: The test is DEFORMATION, not load success. Rig, pose to `victory`, look at the shoulder. Generated topology has no edge loops at joints; if the weights collapse there, the mesh is the ceiling and not the loader.

install._what: In-process, under a second. Copies the rigged glb into assets/ and writes the bone map beside it.
install._map: The map is DATA. install SUGGESTS it from the glb's own joint names and marks it "reviewed": false; the loader warns until a human sets that to true. A wrong guess that runs produces a character that is subtly, unfalsifiably wrong at exactly one joint — worse than a hard stop.
install._bindMode: Omitted, so the loader defaults to "absolute": an unposed clip returns the limbs to the SPEC bind, hanging along −Y. Set "additive" in the bones.json to measure every clip from the glb's own A-pose instead. See the header of src/actors/gltf-actor.js for why absolute is the default and where PLAN-forge.md disagrees.

characters.name: kaida
characters._ref: Human-selected over kaida-plain.png: its legs carry a visible gap, and `plain` merges the thighs into one mass that reconstruction fuses into a single limb.
